To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TS inhibitor, Z D1694, is a highly active drug in human ovarian cancer cell lines, and that it is active in cell lines with acquired cisplatin resistance.
ZD1694 and cisplatin have non-overlapping tumour inhibitory effects and mechanisms of resistance.
the TS inhibitor, ZDD1694, is a potent inhibitor of human tumour growth in vitro and is non-cross-resistant to acquired cisplatin resistance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of resistance to antifolate and platinum-based anticancer drugs and with developing novel agents that overcome such resistance.
the discovery and development of new anticancer agents.
the development of novel antitumour agents, the identification of their mechanisms of action, the development of resistance to these compounds and the design of strategies to overcome resistance.

the TS inhibitors, CB371 and ZD16944, are non-cross-resistant with the platinum drugs, cisplati and JM216.
ZD1694 and the platinum-based drugs are non-cross-resistant in the tumour cell lines investigated, and that their respective mechanisms of tumour resistance also do not overlap.

the antifolates, ZD16944, CB3717 or methotrexate are active in cisplatin resistant cell lines and cisplatin is active in ZD1694 resistant cells.

the TS inhibitor, Z-D1694, and its prototype CB3714, and the DHFR inhibitors, methotrexates, are non-cross resistant to cisplatin, both in sensitive cell lines and in acquired cisplatin resistant cell lines.
